H1.note: one claim per gene with a stated direction: TREM2 R47H raises risk by weakening the response (TREM2 protective), PLCG2 P522R lowers it by raising signalling flux (PLCG2 protective), INPP5D is the brake whose protective allele de-represses the axis (INPP5D raises risk). APOE starts the chain but the run gives it no direction, so no APOE claim. The title names coding variants; the chain starts at proteins, so the claims are about the genes.

H2.note: neither gene's direction on AD is stated outright; read from the mechanism: MS4A4A negatively regulates TREM2 and so weakens the 'TREM2-dependent barrier around plaques' (raises risk), ABI3 executes plaque encapsulation, which H2.4 makes protective (lowers risk). The mechanism states the variants' directions (rs1582763 protective, rs616338 OR 1.31), not the genes'.

H3.note: the title and mechanism give no direction for LPIN2 ('would modify amyloid pathology'); the sign is from the falsification test, which expects the Lpin2 knockout to increase droplet-laden microglia and plaque load. APOE has no stated direction in this hypothesis, so no APOE claim.

H4.no_claim_reason: argues RNPS1 has no causal role in AD (an expression-panel artefact), and the 'if at all' NMD route gives no direction on AD

H5.note: the chain never reaches AD. The mechanism holds two arms of opposite therapeutic sign (INPP5D represses RIPK1-driven inflammation; INPP5D transduces CD22 suppression of Abeta clearance) and names INPP5D's direction on AD as the open question, so there is no AD claim; the two claims target the arms' end nodes.

findings.detail: The run says PMID:41785844 describes MS4A4A elevating TREM2 signalling to reduce amyloid and records the MS4A4A->TREM2 direction as contested; the text says MS4A4A and MS4A6A 'cooperatively restrain TREM2 signaling', the same direction as H2.1, so the contradiction is invented and the citation is evidence for the step.

H2.3 says ABI3 is required for motility, citing Q9P2A4, whose only function text is 'In vitro, reduces cell motility'; the run's own note saw this and kept the opposite sign, resting the step on an uncited WAVE-complex inference.

H1 is 'high' confidence, but of its own chain citations only the STRING APOE-TREM2 edge states a step; H1.2-H1.4 rest on Reactome over-representation and a STRING text-mining edge, H1.6 on variant GWAS rows and a variant-compaction paper, and the only composed arm (INPP5D) borrows H5.3.

The run held text that states H1.2 and H1.3 (PMID:42602355: TREM2 'engages with adaptors like DAP12 ... activating ... PLCγ2') and H1.5 (OT:INPP5D-tractability, UniProt function: 'negatively regulating the PI3K ... pathways') but cited them only at H3.4 and H5.5, and cited enrichment results and STRING edges at the steps instead.

Reactome over-representation results for the gene set (DAP12 interactions/signalling, IP3/IP4 synthesis, NR1H2/NR1H3 pathways) are cited as evidence for directed mechanistic steps; an enrichment says the genes co-occur in a pathway, not that one activates another.

Process->AD steps ('plaque-clearance and compaction program lowers AD', 'encapsulation of plaques lowers AD') cite a variant's GWAS row plus a paper showing the same variant changes plaque compaction; the step is an inference joining two findings, and no cited text states it.

H4.3 asserts RNPS1 associated_with AD citing a GWAS Catalog record of no association and an Open Targets score of 0.01; the run's note concedes the arrow does not exist, so the step should not be in the chain.
H4.2 (NMD lowers INPP5D and PLCG2 transcripts) is marked speculative by the run and cites only RNPS1's UniProt text, which names neither gene.

H5.5 says rosiptor activates INPP5D, but the cited ChEMBL and Open Targets rows say only that rosiptor 'targets' INPP5D; the direction is unsupported, and an activator would deepen the CD22 brake the title's 'disinhibition' implies removing.
H1.4 ends at IP3/Ca2+, H1.5 starts at INPP5D and ends at PI3K signalling, H1.6 starts at the plaque-clearance program: the chain breaks twice, so TREM2 and PLCG2 never reach AD.
Every link breaks: H2.1 ends at TREM2, H2.2 starts at rs1582763 and ends at AD, H2.3 starts at ABI3 and ends at motility, H2.4 starts at plaque encapsulation; the 'chain' is four unrelated facts.

H3.1 ends at phosphatidic acid, H3.2 restarts at LPIN2, H3.3 starts at APOE, H3.4 starts at microglial lipid stress: no step joins LPIN2 or APOE to lipid stress, so the hypothesis's central link is missing.
H4.2 ends at INPP5D/PLCG2 transcripts and H4.3 restarts at RNPS1; the chain has no step from INPP5D or PLCG2 to AD.
H5 is a star around INPP5D, not a chain: H5.3, H5.4 and H5.5 each restart at or end on INPP5D.
No H5 step reaches Alzheimer's disease; the arms end at proinflammatory mediators and Abeta clearance, and the RIPK1 arm has no step to AD anywhere in the run.
H2's mechanism gives directions for the variants (rs1582763 protective, rs616338 OR 1.31) but never for MS4A4A or ABI3 on AD; the curated signs are read through the TREM2 barrier and H2.4.
H3 says LPIN2 'would modify amyloid pathology' with no direction; only the falsification test implies LPIN2 is protective.
Expression levels in microglia (HPA nCPM) are recorded as 'associated_with' a cell type; curated as expressed_in (RO:0002206).

Five steps join two nodes in one label ('IP3/Ca2+', 'plaque-clearance and compaction program', 'motility and process extension', 'NMD and alternative splicing', '(INPP5D, PLCG2)'); split into 13 statements.
H3's contradicting_evidence cites 'GWAS:LPIN2:no-association', and H2's cites 'AGR:MGI:1913860:no-phenotypes'; neither is in sources.json, so neither could be checked.

Supporting citations at no step: STRING:TREM2-INPP5D, STRING:PMID:28714976 (enrichment), rs75932628 (TREM2 R47H, OR 2.22), rs10933431 (INPP5D, OR 0.93), AGR:MGI:1913150:MP:0003691, and three OT disease scores; none states a step, and the variant rows have no variant step to attach to.

Supporting citations at no step: rs11655466 (ABI3 intron variant, OR 1.05), STRING:ABI3-TREM2 (text-mining), Q96JQ5 (MS4A4A 'may be involved in signal transduction'), OT:MS4A4A and OT:ABI3 scores; none states a step. PMID:41785844 did state H2.1 and is attached there.

Supporting citations at no step: three Lpin2 knockout phenotypes (circulating FFA, triglyceride, ataxia), an Apoe knockout astrocyte phenotype and STRING:APOE-TREM2 (used at H1.1); none states an H3 step.

Supporting citations at no step: HPA:ENSG00000205937, OT:RNPS1-constraint and STRING:BTO:0000089 (blood enrichment); none states a step, and they argue against the hypothesis's own NMD route rather than for it.
Supporting citations at no step: rs10933431, two Inpp5d B/T-cell knockout phenotypes, OT:INPP5D-MONDO_0004975 and STRING:INPP5D-PLCG2 (used at H1.5); none states an H5 step.

The one fetched contradicting citation (PMID:42601455) agrees with H1 on direction (PLCG2 loss raises AD risk); it contradicts only the cell type (neurons, not microglia), which the run states correctly.
BLN:AmyloidPlaqueCompaction: no GO process for compaction of amyloid plaques (H1.6).
BLN:MicroglialPlaqueEncapsulation: no term for microglia encapsulating or forming a barrier around plaques (H2.4).
BLN:MicroglialLipidStress: no term for lipid stress or the lipid-droplet-accumulating microglial state (H3.4); 'response to lipid' is a stimulus response, not the state.

The 'plaque-clearance' part of H1.6 and H5.3's 'microglial amyloid-beta clearance' are merged as GO:0097242; H1's only composed arm (INPP5D -> Abeta clearance -> AD) depends on this merge and borrows H5.3.
A null hypothesis ('RNPS1 has no causal role in AD') cannot be stated: claims need a sign, so the hypothesis's actual claim is recorded only as no_claim_reason.
A hypothesis that asserts two arms of opposite sign on the disease and leaves the net sign open has no claim form; recorded as two end-node claims and no AD claim.

Evidence bearing directly on a hypothesis claim (PMID:42601455: PLCG2 LoF variants raise AD risk tenfold) has nowhere to go when no step states it; a claim cannot carry evidence, and a bridge equal to the whole claim is not a bridge.

UniProt's 'Involved in X' (participation) counts as undirected under the guide, so the commonest UniProt wording never supports a required_for step; a participates_in rel (RO:0000056) would hold it but is not what the step claims.
The kind table has no row for an HPA single-cell expression level as evidence for 'expressed in'; used observational.
PMID:41435829 perturbs MS4A4A in non-human primates and mice; taxa have no primate, so the evidence is tagged mouse.
PMID:42582107 uses 'primary microglia' without a species; with no taxon the evidence reads as human, and there is no 'unknown' taxon.

The INPP5D record the run cited (OT:INPP5D-tractability, UniProt function) says INPP5D hydrolyzes 1D-myo-inositol 1,4,5-trisphosphate and modulates phospholipase C activity, the direct biochemical link between the 'brake' and the PLCG2 arm; H1 never uses it and instead routes INPP5D through PI3K signalling, which joins nothing.

One STRING edge (S1) or one UniProt function line (S6), both curatedDb, reach 'established' (b 4/5), while MS4A4A -> TREM2 (S9), backed by an in vivo knockout/antibody study in mice and NHPs plus a review, stops at b 23/29 'unsupported' because of the taxon discount.

Splitting a compound subject (NMD and alternative splicing) over a listed object (INPP5D, PLCG2) gives four statements for one step, each excluding the same citation, so one citation judgement counts four times.
